Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

recognize verb

acknowledge, admit

also acknowledge, admit, own up, I admit, I must admit

classical

Cic. Fam. 4.4.1: mē nōn esse verbōrum admodum inopem agnōscō
Cic. Fam. 5.20.5: id ego agnōvī meō jussū esse factum

agnōscō, agnōscere, agnōvī, agnitum

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

acknowledge, own (as one’s own or as true)

Lewis & Short: to acknowledge a thing as one’s own, a deed, a debt, a child, a fault (culpam agnōscere, see accept blame); with an accusative and infinitive, to admit that.

Other words

  • fateor, fatērī, fassus sum — admit, confess; said in passing, “I admit”

    verb, second conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 158: ita rēs est, fateor; Cic. Att. 2.1.5: fateor; sed ego illam ōdī · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Usually with an accusative and infinitive (Lewis & Short).

  • cōnfiteor, cōnfitērī, cōnfessus sum — confess, own up to

    verb, second conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. N.D. 2.11 (Lewis & Short): peccātum suum · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short: of owning to an error or to something denied before, at some cost to one’s will; fateor is a plain acknowledgement.

Examples

  • et ego ipse … mē nōn esse verbōrum admodum inopem agnōscō

    and I myself admit that I am not altogether short of wordsCic. Fam. 4.4.1

  • Ita rēs est, fateor: peccātum ā mē maximum est.

    That is how it is, I admit: I have done a very great wrong.Ter. Heaut. 158

  • Ego mē amāre hanc fateor: sī id peccāre est, fateor id quoque.

    I admit that I love her; if that is a sin, I admit that too.Ter. And. 896

See also accept blame, recognize, agree, true.
